newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Askari Bank up on credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Askari Bank up on credit rating.

text.p: Pakistan's Askari Commercial Bank jumped 1.10 rupees, or 5.24 percent, to 22.10 at the Karachi Stock Exchange on Sunday after a local credit rating agency gave it high ratings, dealers said.

Dealer Manocher Jamal of Taurus Securities said some 78,000 Askari shares changed hands in brisk morning trading after the Pakistan Credit Rating Agency (PACRA) assigned the bank a short-term rating of A1+ and a long-term rating of A+.
"The stock's price is likely to close higher," he said.
The credit rating agency said details of the ratings would be released later.
"The rating of A1+ is the highest in the short-term category and stands for obligations supported by the highest capacity for timely repayment," said an Askari Bank executive.
The executive, who asked not to be named, said Askari, partly owned by the Army Welfare Trust, was the first private Pakistani bank to get such a high rating.
